jobs.title: VP, Engineering
jobs.description:
1Password is growing.
We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

The Vice President of Platform Engineering reports to the CTO and leads the strategy, organization, and execution for 1Password’s core service and development platforms. The VP is accountable for building secure, reliable, and scalable foundations that enable teams across 1Password to deliver, operate, and own with autonomy, speed, and unambiguous accountability. The VP owns operations, drives delivery, and develops a high-performing team to achieve impactful results.

How We’re Using AI Today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What We're Looking For

Experience: 10+ years of experience in software engineering, with at least 7 years in a leadership role, preferably with experience building and operating at the intersections of IaaS, SaaS, and the cybersecurity industry.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, or related fields; or proven equivalent work experience.
Proven track record establishing durable, full-lifecycle ownership for critical platforms and services, including adoption, customer experience, reliability, security, cost, incident response, and continued evolution.
Proven ability delivering and operating cost-effective mission-critical infrastructure and platform systems serving internal- and consumer-facing software products, operational efficiency and market expansion.
Strong business and technical acumen in systems and software engineering, proven ability to lead an organization and culture delivering best practices and innovation.
Exceptional analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to define, develop and execute strategic plans across a wide set of objectives, driving committed quantifiable results.
Extensive experience in building, maintaining, and influencing operational excellence, including process and system optimization, scalability, and the development and management of performance metrics
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with C-suite leaders and cross-functional teams, aligning on strategic priorities to achieve shared objectives.
Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly, build trust, inspire broadly, gaining alignment across diverse stakeholders.
Proven expertise in leading and sustaining multi-year transformational initiatives in fast-paced, complex, and dynamic environments.
Proven experience building, developing and scaling high-performing teams.

What You Can Expect

Leadership: Continuously evolve, develop and execute the Platform Engineering vision, strategy, objectives, and roadmaps, aligning and laddering it with the company strategy and customer needs. Proactively incorporate market and industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer insights to identify opportunities, informing strategic decision-making.
Transformation: Lead multi-year changes to 1Password’s engineering architecture and operating model, building shared platforms, supported paths, and common practices that improve reliability, security, developer effectiveness, and the company’s ability to scale.
Company Initiatives: Lead technology-adjacent strategic initiatives that facilitate delivering best-in-class engineering results, from inspiration and innovation, to implementation and iterative improvement.
Operations: Design and evolve the organization, ownership model, and operating mechanisms needed to execute the strategy. Establish clear accountability for the platforms and services the organization operates directly, while creating governed, supported paths that enable other teams to own and operate their products independently.
Engineering Systems and Practices: Advance how software is built and operated across 1Password through ubiquitous engineering standards, operational excellence, and safe, measurable Agentic Engineering practices. Establish the platforms, controls, and evidence needed for teams to adopt these practices while remaining accountable for their results.
Performance: Establish clear, quantifiable outcomes across the organization and operating mechanisms that expose progress, quality, adoption, operational health, and business impact. Use evidence to make investment, prioritization, and organizational decisions, transparently providing actionable insights for the executive team and organizational leaders.
Cross-functional Collaboration: Build strong relationships across the company to proactively identify needs, align strategies, and optimize your company-wide impact. Foster collaboration within and beyond the Technology organization to influence change. Apply critical feedback toward achieving strategic goals. Represent the technical organization in senior leadership meetings, providing updates on strategic initiatives, operational execution, and industry trends and their implications.
Team Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team by mentoring and coaching direct reports, evaluating organizational talent, and implementing plans to prepare talent for future business demands.
Leadership Growth: Invest in the growth and development of the leaders within the technology organization across 1Password via direct mentorship, sponsorship, and participation at sibling organization events, as well as providing leadership alongside cross-functional partner teams, such as Product, Security, People/Talent, Operations and L&D.
Culture and Org Health: Drive and evolve our high-performance culture, fostering psychological safety, inclusivity, ownership, and agility. Champion initiatives to enhance the employee experience organizationally- and company-wide.
Financial Oversight: In partnership with Finance, own the organization’s investment and capacity strategy, balancing current operations, future-state transformation, and targeted growth. Ensure resources are allocated against the highest-value outcomes and adjust plans when evidence or business priorities change.

USA-based roles: The annual base salary for this role is between $302,000 USD and $483,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles: The annual base salary for this role is between $278,000 CAD and $445,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture

At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How We Work With AI

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work

We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What We Offer

We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

🩺 Competitive health benefits

Location

Technology Services

Technology Services (TS) is responsible for delivering all enterprise infrastructure, applications and related end user technology services across all Brookfield business groups.

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

The Director, Enterprise Architecture is a strategic technology leadership role responsible for connecting business objectives, enterprise platforms, infrastructure services, cloud environments, security, networking, operations, and application development into a cohesive technology ecosystem.

This leader will serve as a cross-functional architecture authority, partnering with all technology towers to ensure solutions are scalable, secure, integrated, operationally sustainable, and aligned with the Company’s long-term technology strategy.

The position will help align stakeholders, coordinate technical dependencies across towers, facilitate solution decisions, and ensure enterprise-wide execution alignment for strategic programs and projects.

The role requires a highly experienced technology professional with broad enterprise architecture expertise, strong business acumen, and the ability to influence technical and operational teams across the organization. This position will work closely with Cloud, Security, Network, End User Services, Application teams, and PMO leadership to drive architecture governance, modernization initiatives, integration strategies, and enterprise-wide technology standards

Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.
As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,700 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!

Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As the Director, Enterprise Architecture
, you will provide strategic and people leadership for Vancity’s architecture practice, shaping the technology architecture required to deliver our business and technology strategies. You will lead and develop a team of architects responsible for defining scalable, resilient, secure, and future-ready solutions across the organization, while establishing architectural direction, standards, governance, and practices that ensure technology investments align with Vancity’s long-term business priorities. You will work closely with senior technology and business leaders to translate strategy into technology roadmaps, guide major transformation initiatives, and ensure architectural decisions balance innovation, sustainability, risk, scalability, and business value. As a people leader, you will build capability within the architecture team, establish clear accountabilities and expectations, coach and develop team members, and foster a collaborative and high-performing architecture practice.
This is a Full-time, Permanent
role and will report directly to the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture and Transformation.
This role will enjoy hybrid working arrangements which can be fulfilled primarily from the Vancity head office location and your Lower Mainland based home office or Toronto home based office. Vancouver-based candidates may be expected to come into office at least once per week.

How You'll Make an Impact:

Leading
, coaching, and developing a team of architects, providing clear direction, performance expectations, career development, and opportunities to strengthen technical and leadership capabilities

Providing
strategic leadership and architectural direction for key business and technology initiatives, ensuring solutions align with Vancity’s enterprise strategy and long-term technology vision

Defining
, building, and maintaining architecture standards, principles, patterns, guardrails, and best practices, while establishing effective architecture governance and decision-making practices across the organization

Partnering
with senior business and technology leaders to understand business drivers, capabilities, and strategic priorities and translating them into technology strategies, roadmaps, and architectural outcomes

Providing
leadership and direction to solution, data, security, infrastructure, and other architecture disciplines, ensuring architectural decisions are aligned across the technology ecosystem

Guiding
product owners, engineering leaders, architects, designers, and developers in making sound architecture choices, including Buy vs. Build, cloud adoption, integration patterns, and real-time vs. batch solutions

Overseeing
the design and implementation of solutions across business applications and technologies based on enterprise strategy, business capabilities, security requirements, and technology standards

Providing
leadership and architectural oversight for significant transformation programs and complex technology initiatives, identifying cross-functional dependencies, risks, opportunities, and architectural considerations

Monitoring
the current-state technology portfolio and establishing roadmaps to address technical debt, aging technologies, regulatory requirements, architectural deficiencies, and misalignment with evolving business requirements

Evaluating
emerging technologies, including AI, automation, cloud platforms, modern engineering practices, fintech trends, vendor capabilities, and market changes to determine how they can responsibly enable new business capabilities and operating models

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

10+ years of progressive technology experience, including significant experience in solution and enterprise architecture, ideally within financial services or banking environments

Demonstrated experience leading, managing, coaching, and developing architecture or senior technology teams, with accountability for performance, capability development, and delivery

Current expertise in AI, including AI-enabled architecture, AI governance, and AI spec-driven development, combined with broad knowledge of software architecture, application development, data, security, infrastructure, cloud computing, automation, and modern engineering practices

Experience establishing or maturing an architecture practice, including architecture governance, standards, principles, roadmaps, and decision-making frameworks

Strong experience influencing senior executives and business leaders and translating business strategy into technology strategy and architectural direction

Experience with cloud architecture, preferably Microsoft Azure, along with in-depth knowledge of integration patterns, APIs, microservices, event-driven architectures, and modern application architecture

Strong people leadership, communication, analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to create clarity, build alignment, navigate competing priorities, and provide direction in complex or ambiguous environments

Extra Skills That Set You Apart:

Experience with modern core banking systems and a strong understanding of the banking and fintech technology landscape

Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks and methodologies, such as TOGAF, and the ability to apply architecture practices pragmatically within a complex organization

Familiarity with Agile and modern product and software development practices and experience partnering with product and engineering leaders

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are:

A people leader who builds strong teams
- You set clear expectations, coach and develop others, create accountability, and build an environment where experienced technology professionals can do their best work.

A big-picture technology strategist
- You can translate complex business strategies into practical, scalable enterprise architectures and long-term technology roadmaps.

A trusted leader and collaborator
- You can influence senior leaders, bring together different perspectives, and provide clear direction when architectural decisions involve competing priorities or trade-offs.

Fluent in both business and technology
- You connect business drivers, member outcomes, capabilities, risk, and strategy to architectural and investment decisions.

Comfortable leading through complexity and change
- You can provide clarity in ambiguous environments while helping your team and stakeholders navigate transformation, emerging technologies, and evolving business priorities.

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don't perfectly align with those listed.

What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of $180,000 to $200,000 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:

About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Represent FX Engineering in executive committees, architecture forums, regulatory reviews, and transformation governance bodies.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.
ROLE DESCRIPTION

Financial Accounting and Reporting

· Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
· Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
· Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
· Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
· Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
· Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
· Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
· Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.
Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

· Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
· Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
· Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
· Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
· Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.
Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

· Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
· Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
· Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
· Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
· Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
· Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.
Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

· Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
· Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.

· Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
· Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.

Other

Description

We are seeking an experienced and entrepreneurial Managing Director
to lead one of our software businesses within TAG Software Group. As MD, you will own the P&L, set strategic direction, and drive sustained growth and profitability across the business.

Success will be measured by outcomes, raising operational excellence, scaling customer success, and building high-performing leadership teams that multiply impact. This position provides critical operational leadership to a company and potentially a portfolio of companies within a growing software vertical.

About Tag Software Group

TAG Software Group is a team of experienced investors and operators dedicated to acquiring, enhancing, and growing mission-critical software companies serving SMB, enterprise, and public sector customers.

Founded as part of a permanent home for software companies, we don’t buy to sell. Our focus is on long-term partnerships that protect your legacy, employees, and customers.

Our in-house team delivers an efficient, transparent, and seller-friendly process, ensuring speed and certainty of close. Once part of TAG, your company gains access to proven best practices, dedicated value-creation resources, and the extended ecosystem of our sister companies, including proprietary in-house technology including and — helping your business reach the next level.

Investment Approach

Unlike private equity and venture capital firms, we are Entrepreneurs who Buy, Enhance and Grow Software Businesses. That’s right; we don’t sell businesses. We form a strategic alliance with existing management teams. We recognize the dedication and perseverance required to create a firm and place a premium on customers’ and workers’ well-being over short-term goals.

Culture

Tag Software Group is more than just a place to work; we’re a team. We mean it when we say people are our greatest assets, so investing in them is our number one priority. We create an environment where our employees feel first-day-on-the-job excitement, day after day, creating a culture of high performers and collaboration. We celebrate our milestones, and we’re proud of them. We Dream Big, Stay Humble, and Stay Hungry.

Position Description

As Managing Director, you will provide strategic, operational, and financial leadership to a software business or portfolio within the Tag Software Group family. You will develop and implement the business strategy across sales, marketing, R&D, customer service, professional services, and HR. Working with the Business Unit leadership team, you will set growth objectives, lead execution, and drive operational excellence.

You will be fully accountable for business performance, profitability, scalability, and long-term customer and employee success.

Key Responsibilities

Achieve sustainable business growth by positioning the company strategically within its markets and aligning operations with long-term objectives.
Deliver measurable improvements in scalability, efficiency, and operational excellence across the business.
Drive consistent revenue growth through effective market expansion, cross-selling, and customer-focused strategies.
Ensure customer satisfaction and loyalty remain strong, supporting high retention and advocacy.
Maintain clear, market-aligned product strategies and roadmaps that balance innovation with stability, supporting both new customer acquisition and retention.
Foster an environment of innovation and technology adoption, challenging the status quo and leveraging emerging tools (including AI) to improve products, services, and operations.
Own full P&L responsibility, ensuring revenue growth, profitability, financial discipline, and long-term resilience.
Translate deep financial insight into strategic and operational decisions that maximize value creation.
Meet or exceed key performance metrics including revenue, EBITDA, ROI, and customer retention.
Optimize capital allocation and ensure predictable financial performance across monthly, quarterly, and annual periods.
Build and sustain high-performing teams capable of delivering exceptional results across all functions.
Create a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement that enhances both individual and organizational performance.
Inspire, motivate, and develop teams to achieve ambitious milestones and exceed expectations.
Lead confidently through change, simplifying complexity, removing roadblocks, and executing strategies that deliver long-term business success.
Represent Tag Software Group leadership values by demonstrating humility, empathy, strategic judgment, and an entrepreneurial mindset in all decisions.

Requirements

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Proven ability to own a P&L and deliver sustained growth, profitability, and scalability.
Track record of driving market expansion, launching new products, or transforming businesses.
Strong financial acumen and ability to make value-creating decisions.
Experience building and leading executive-level teams.
Comfort with emerging technologies (including AI).
Exceptional communication and influence skills.
Ability to simplify complexity, work through ambiguity, and make bold decisions.
Resilience and adaptability under pressure.

Additional Or Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience managing a B2B software company.
Proven entrepreneurial mindset and pace-setter traits.
Bachelor’s degree (MBA or advanced degree a plus).
8+ years of cross-functional leadership experience with P&L ownership.
Broad financial understanding (P&L, BI tools, FP&A, financial documents).
Experience developing strategies for customer acquisition and market penetration.
Ability to analyze and solve complex business problems.
Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Benefits

WHY JOIN US:

Lead an established software company with the backing of a global acquisition group.
High autonomy within a decentralized operating structure.
Opportunity to shape and scale a business for long-term success.
Career growth within a rapidly expanding, entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Remote work flexibility (location-dependent).

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. This role ensures accurate and timely accounting, compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, effective cash and balance sheet management, and robust internal controls. They will be responsible for all day-to-day finance operations, including functional responsibility over general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, pension administration, treasury, investments.
The Director of Finance is responsible for audit readiness by ensuring robust policies, systems, and procedures are in place, and by supporting the external audit process as required.
In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.
ROLE DESCRIPTION

Financial Accounting and Reporting

· Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
· Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
· Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
· Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
· Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
· Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
· Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
· Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.
Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

· Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
· Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
· Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
· Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
· Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.
Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

· Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
· Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
· Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
· Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
· Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
· Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.
Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

· Oversee daily cash management, bank relationships, and banking structures.
· Ensure appropriate controls over cash receipts, disbursements, and account reconciliations.
· Monitor liquidity and working capital from an operational and control perspective, in alignment with CFO direction.
· Authorize banking arrangements and ensure compliance with signing authorities and delegated limits outlined in the Organizational Authority Registrar.
Investments Oversight (Outsourced Chief Investment Officer Governance)

· Provide financial governance and oversight of ESA’s investment activities managed by an outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO), in accordance with approved investment policies, mandates, and governance frameworks.
· Act as the secondary finance liaison with the OCIO to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of investment‑related financial information and reporting. The CFO is the primary point of contact for investment-related activities.
· Review and assess investment valuations, and accounting treatments prepared under the OCIO’s management for compliance with applicable accounting standards and investment policies.
· Monitor adherence to internal controls related to investment transactions, custody, valuation, and financial disclosures, including controls executed by the OCIO and third‑party service providers.
· Coordinate with the OCIO, custodians, external managers, actuaries (where applicable), and auditors to support audit activities and regulatory reporting related to investments.
· Ensure appropriate investment disclosures are prepared for financial statements
· Support the CFO and relevant board committee by conducting a detailed review of quarterly reports provided by the outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO). This includes assessing the completeness, accuracy, and clarity of reporting related to portfolio performance, asset allocation, valuation methodologies, compliance with the Investment Policy Statement, and key risk exposures.
· Liaise with the OCIO to obtain clarifications, supplemental analysis, or follow‑up information as required to support informed oversight and governance discussions at the committee level.
Pension and Other Post Employment Benefits Accounting

· Oversee accounting, reporting, and compliance related to pension plans and post‑employment benefits.
· Liaise with external actuaries, pension administrators, and external auditors on valuation, disclosures, and funding matters.
· Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
· Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.
Payroll

· Provide strategic leadership and oversight over ESA’s payroll function, with operational payroll processing executed by senior payroll professionals.
· Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
· Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.
· Ensure robust internal controls are designed, implemented, and operating effectively over payroll processing, payroll changes, reconciliations, and access management to ESA’s payroll system.
· Oversee payroll accounting and financial integrity, including review of payroll reconciliations and confirmation of accurate recording of payroll‑related expenses, liabilities, and accruals.
· Review and challenge escalated payroll issues, exceptions, or control matters, approving resolution approaches and escalating material risks to the CFO as appropriate.
· Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives related to payroll systems, processes, controls, and reporting to enhance efficiency, risk management, and employee experience.
People Management:

· Lead, mentor, and develop a high performing finance team.
· Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement and customer service to cross-functional business units
Other

· Effectively represent the Finance team as a Senior Management Team Member on board committees or internal committees as required.
QUALIFICATIONS

• CPA designation required
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
· At least 10-12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance.
· Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable, accounts receivable, investments and pension accounting.
• Experience supervising a team of finance professionals.
• Experience with non-government not for profit accounting and a solid knowledge and
understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.
• Analytic, organization, and problem-solving skills for strategic data interpretation.
• Strong emotional intelligence and self-awareness is essential.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills required to effectively communicate complex
issues to senior leadership.
• The ability to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.
• Requires demonstrated listening and negotiating skills and the ability to work effectively with people inside and outside the organization to achieve the required results.

The practice is home to a technically gifted, close-knit team of senior designers and planners who care deeply about their craft and about the communities they serve. Demand for the firm’s work is steady, its reputation is excellent, and its people are proud of what they build. The organization now looks to formalize how it is led and to bring dedicated business leadership to a practice whose creative strength has always been its foundation.

The Opportunity

This is the senior-most role in the practice, and a rare one in the Winnipeg market. The Managing Director takes full ownership of the firm as a business, with real autonomy over direction, structure, and results, and complete accountability for profit and loss. Where leaders at larger national firms often run a department within a corporate structure, this role runs the whole enterprise, shaping its strategy, its culture, and its next generation of leaders.

The incoming leader will work alongside a talented group of principals and design professionals, earning their confidence, strengthening how decisions get made, and bringing greater commercial discipline to how projects are scoped, priced, tracked, and delivered. There is meaningful design work ahead: shaping the firm’s organizational structure in partnership with the team, putting a newly developed strategic plan into motion, and building a clear path for emerging leaders. A thoughtful ramp-up is built in, so the right person can learn the business and build relationships before the real work begins. This role is based in the Winnipeg office, five days a week, with periodic travel to a satellite location.

Key Responsibilities

Run the practice as a self-directed business, setting priorities, owning financial results, and reporting at a high level to ownership on a quarterly basis.
Lead, coach, and develop a group of senior principals, fostering alignment and shared accountability, addressing difficult conversations directly and respectfully, and cultivating the next generation of firm leadership.
Take over the full range of people leadership, including compensation reviews, performance conversations, workforce planning, and the retention and engagement of a talented professional team.
Instill financial discipline across the practice, including utilization and chargeability, project pricing and margins, and rigorous tracking of scope and change, so that decisions are guided by sound numbers as well as sound design judgment.
Co-design the firm’s organizational structure with the leadership team, and lead execution of the new strategic plan across the practice.
Support senior-level business development alongside the principals who lead client relationships, represent the firm in the community, and provide a light-touch, growth-minded presence for the satellite office.

Qualifications

A background in architecture, engineering, landscape architecture, planning, land development, or a closely related design and consulting field, with enough depth in the industry to earn the respect of senior technical professionals.
A proven record of building teams and leading collaboratively, paired with the confidence to set direction and make decisions when the situation calls for it.
Demonstrated comfort with hard conversations and conflict resolution, with the interpersonal maturity to guide experienced, long-tenured professionals through change.
Strong business and financial acumen, including hands-on experience with P&L ownership, utilization, project pricing, and margin management in a project-based professional services environment.
The ability to win work, build relationships with clients and partners, and represent the firm credibly within the Winnipeg business and design community.
Winnipeg-based, with the ability to work on site five days a week; leaders currently running practices at larger firms who are seeking genuine autonomy are encouraged to apply.
